clue.text: 100 ring over voucher

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a ring is round like the letter O
over and upon both mean on top of

explanation.surface: A hundred-pound ring offered against a voucher, as if in a shop promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a printed slip exchanged for goods or a discount, which is exactly what a voucher is.

clue.text: Cyclist initially spots collision

indicators.note: initially points to the very start of the neighbouring word, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of Cyclist
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A cyclist sees the danger only at the start, just before a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a violent impact between vehicles, the same thing as a collision.

clue.text: Miserable out at fen, run off

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled or gone wrong, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone left out on the fens feels miserable and runs away.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfortunate person is unlucky and wretched, so the word can stand for miserable as an adjective.

clue.text: Get the better of me, giving support to accomplished commander

parts.note: something accomplished is finished, or over
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer gives in to the speaker while supporting a decorated commander.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'giving support to' puts the first piece underneath the rest, so it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to defeat them, which is what getting the better of means.

clue.text: Blackleg at pub confronting duke that carries a sword

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: the thing that carries a sword

parts.note: a blackleg or scab is a worker who breaks a strike
a bar is a pub
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker in a pub squares up to a duke who is armed with a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confronting' just places the pub before the duke in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath in which a sword is carried at the hip.

clue.text: Independent member, more peevish about form?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps itself round the other

parts.note: crosser means angrier, more peevish
a form is a long backless bench, as in a school

explanation.surface: An independent politician gets grumpier about the official paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a document, but here it is the old school bench. A crossbencher sits in the House of Lords without belonging to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbenchers are peers aligned with no party, so each is an independent member of the House of Lords.

clue.text: German chap in outskirts of Benidorm, the far end

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the remaining pair of letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Benidorm
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German man stays on the edge of the Spanish resort, at the far end of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Benidorm is a Spanish holiday resort popular with Britons.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom of a garden or street is its far end, the part furthest away.

clue.text: Very good air conditioning at top of escalator

parts.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for air conditioning

indicators.note: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of escalator

explanation.surface: Cool air blowing at the top of a shop escalator is very welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace is informal praise meaning excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Treacherously abandon sailor sent over for WWII soldier

parts.note: to desert is to abandon a post or duty in betrayal

indicators.note: something sent over is turned the other way, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to betray his comrades by abandoning a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division fighting in North Africa during the Second World War.

clue.text: Former king of France in crooked deal

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other
a crooked deal is bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to rearrange
FR is the abbreviation for France

explanation.surface: A deposed French king is caught up in a shady deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former king of France' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'king'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century king of Wessex, so he is a king of the past.

clue.text: Beneficial to lock stronghold

parts.note: something for you is good for you
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A good lock would help a fortified place stay secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door fastening, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a fortified military building, the same as a stronghold.

clue.text: Squaddie is in a Coward play

parts.note: a squaddie is a private soldier, British slang
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A soldier is cast in a play, or else is a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward wrote Private Lives (1930); 'Coward' looks like an insult to the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Lives is a famous comedy by the English playwright Noel Coward.

clue.text: Wren seen by parsley and baneberry?

parts.note: parsley is an example of a herb
Sir Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A small bird is spotted beside some parsley and a poisonous berry in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen by' sets the parsley next to the architect; the question mark flags the obscure plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Christopher is an old common name for the baneberry, a woodland plant with toxic berries.

clue.text: Thick-skinned creature joining royal in ancient city

parts.note: the hippopotamus is famously thick-skinned
Regius is Latin for royal, as in a Regius professor

explanation.surface: A hippo joins a royal party visiting an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippo Regius was a Roman-era city in North Africa, home of St Augustine.

clue.text: Sad one inside proposes showing pornographic films

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad

indicators.note: inside places the single letter within the following word

parts.note: to move a motion is to propose it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lonely person proposes a night of watching adult films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' also means smutty, which is the sense in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue movies is an idiom for pornographic films, blue being slang for indecent.

clue.text: Restaurant could make money by lake

parts.note: brass is slang for money, especially in northern England
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A restaurant by the lakeside could be a nice earner.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant.

clue.text: Pole rebukes revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke them

explanation.surface: A Polish man scolds a political rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish person, but the definition is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Head of government department, one entering large church

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church, such as York Minster
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A government chief walks into a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a minister is the politician in charge of a government department.

clue.text: A container, slightly open

parts.note: taken as written
a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A tin or box whose lid has been left slightly open.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is partly open rather than shut.

clue.text: Persevere to the end with one solicitor, after criticism

parts.note: to take stick is to be criticised
I is the Roman numeral one
a tout is one who solicits custom

explanation.surface: After harsh criticism a client sticks with their lawyer to the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After criticism' puts that piece first. 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits business, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick it out is an idiom for enduring something difficult until it is over.

clue.text: Small, most of brood left within

indicators.note: within places the single letter inside the shortened word
most of means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Most of the young have left the nest, leaving the small ones inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Little and small are straightforward synonyms describing limited size.

clue.text: What a courier may have brought that a spinner hopes to produce?

definitions.text: What a courier may have brought
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a parcel sent by an express postal service

definitions.text: that a spinner hopes to produce
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an exceptional ball bowled in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a bowler who spins the ball, and each ball bowled is a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an express postal service and, punningly, a superb ball from a slow bowler.

clue.text: Food supplement, of course, that includes a bit of torula

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it inside itself

parts.note: of course is an emphatic yes
taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here its first

parts.note: first letter of torula

explanation.surface: A dietary supplement which naturally contains a little torula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' does double duty in the surface but is just the letter to insert. Torula is in fact a yeast-like fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast, as brewer's or nutritional yeast, is taken as a vitamin-rich food supplement.

clue.text: Corresponding with an uncle, perhaps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a member of one's family

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up letters with their uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponding' suggests writing letters, but it is the sense of being in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative as an adjective means proportionate or comparable; as a noun it is a family member, an uncle being one example.

clue.text: Sauce from packet mostly used up

indicators.note: in a down answer going up means the letters are read from the bottom
mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a packet and a pile are both informal for a large sum of money

explanation.surface: The sauce from the sachet has nearly all been used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks culinary but means cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip and sauce are both informal words for cheeky, impertinent talk.

clue.text: The Scourge of God held back by Vandal? It tallies

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
held means kept inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of Vandal and run through the next two words

explanation.surface: A historian checks that a barbarian sacker of Rome fits the famous nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vandal' suggests the Germanic tribe, fitting the scene, but it only hosts letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun was called the Scourge of God by Christian chroniclers for his devastating invasions.

clue.text: Coffee service finally provided — put in large cupboard

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: last letter of service

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: so, as in 'so long as', means provided that
a press is a large cupboard, as for linen

explanation.surface: At the end of the meal service, coffee is provided and the cups go back in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Cheers for model

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
to sit for a painter is to model

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers for model' sounds like applause for a fashion model, but it splits as for + model.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin drinking toast, used exactly as cheers is.
